We propose a fully convolutional one-stage object detector (FCOS) to solve object detection in a per-pixel prediction fashion, analogue to semantic segmentation. In contrast, our proposed detector FCOS is anchor box free, as well as proposal free. citations.section_path: Bridging the Gap Between Anchor-based and Anchor-free Detection via Adaptive Training Sample Selection / Abstract
citations.excerpt:
## Abstract

Object detection has been dominated by anchor-based detectors for several years. Recently, anchor-free detectors have become popular due to the proposal of FPN and Focal Loss. In this paper, we first point out that the essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is actually how to define positive and negative training samples, which leads to the performance gap between them. If they adopt the same definition of positive and negative samples during training, there is no obvious difference in the final performance, no matter regressing from a box or a point.

## 1 INTRODUCTION

Object recognition is one of the fundamental challenges in computer vision.
